newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss energy moves leave merger chances unclear.
newsitem.headline: Swiss energy moves leave merger chances unclear.

text.p: The chances of a mega-merger of Swiss electrical utilities at the heart of Europe's power networks remained uncertain on Monday despite a reshuffling of holdings by two of Switzerland's biggest banks, analysts said.

After over a year of fevered speculation about a utilities merger, the Swiss stock market reacted with disappointment that key power groups Aare-Tessin AG fuer Elektrizitaet (Atel) and EG Laufenburg remained in separate hands.

At issue was the sale of a 40 percent stake in Atel's majority owner Motor-Columbus by Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS) and the creation of a new utilities group including Laufenburg by its parent, Elektrowatt.
"The fact that stock prices fell today shows that the market is giving up its fantasies about a merger," analyst Andre Bellaggio at Zurich Cantonal Bank said.
Shares fell in most of the utilities involved as well as in UBS and CS Holding, parent of Credit Suisse bank and holder of a 44.9 percent stake in Elektrowatt.

Both UBS and CS Holding have long said they wanted to sell their non-bank holdings, sparking speculation that Atel would be merged with Laufenburg and possibly Elektrowatt's three other Swiss power producers.
"It is more likley now that a third party, some big European group, will step in to take a large share of Laufenburg or Atel," Ballagio added.

While some analysts and traders agreed that chances for a merger had been laid to rest, at least for the short term, others argued that market forces would continue to push for a union of Atel and Laufenburg.
Both Atel and Laufenburg are major European players in electricity trading, the business of moving power from producers in one part of Europe to users elsewhere.

Both also have large and complimentary distribution lines strategically placed at the heart of a growing power trade between northern and southern Europe -- Atel over the Alps to power importer Italy, and Laufenburg to exporter Germany.

"A merger still makes sense if you want to strengthen the Swiss position in a field that is becoming increasingly competitive as Europe deregulates the power sector," said Beat Kunz at Bank Julius Baer.
"It is still conceivable," he said about a merger.

"Atel and EG Laufenburg would be Europe's biggest power trader by volume if they merged," Kunz said, adding that synergies could save up to 20 million Swiss francs ($15.26 million) a year in a sector where margins are under pressure from competition and over-production.

Atel posted sales of 1.57 billion Swiss francs in 1995 and a net profit of 157 million. Laufenburg had sales of 911 million Swiss francs in the 1995/96 year that ended on September 30 and a profit of 32.9 million.

But those who see less chance of a merger said UBS's weekend sale of a large part of its stake in Motor-Columbus cemented an atmosphere of ill-will towards CS Holding caused by an abortive takeover offer for UBS by CS last April.

UBS on Sunday said it was selling two stakes of 20 percent each to state utility Electricite de France International SA (EDF) and Germany's RWE. It will remain the biggest Motor-Columbus shareholder by keeping another 35.6 percent stake.

Elektrowatt said late on Friday it was spinning off its utilities business as a separate company to be named Watt AG, with CS Holding keeping a stake of 44.9 percent in both Elektrowatt and Watt. ($1=1.3108 Swiss Franc)
